clue.text: Such games endlessly held, oddly, in Athenian surroundings

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for Athenian

parts.note: Attic means of Athens or Attica

indicators.note: oddly says the remaining letters are arranged in a strange order
endlessly says the printed word held loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone describes games staged, strangely, against a classical Greek backdrop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts held to HEL, 'oddly' scrambles that to HLE, and 'in' puts HLE inside ATTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Track and field contests are called athletic events or sports, so the adjective describes such games.

clue.text: One hoping to see our island in dry circumstances?

indicators.note: in circumstances places the words inside the dry letters

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so dry
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sightseer hopes to visit our island even when it is alcohol-free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ... circumstances' puts OUR plus IS inside TT, teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: A holidaymaker goes to a place to take in its sights.

clue.text: Gin additive freely dispensed in Chinatown

parts.note: lime juice is added to gin in a gimlet
drinks given free are on the house

explanation.surface: A bar in the Chinese quarter of a city gives away gin mixers.
explanation.walkthrough: This East London district by the docks was London's first Chinatown.
explanation.definitionFit: The East London dockland district was home to London's original Chinese community.

clue.text: It swims quietly round in a mountain lake?

indicators.note: in puts the two small pieces inside the lake word

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
p (piano) means quietly in music
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Something swims silently in circles in an upland lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A large silvery game fish of warm Atlantic waters is a swimmer.

clue.text: We have 'some old relations in Kent, by the way

definitions.text: We have 'some old relations in Kent, by the way

parts.words: We have 'some old relations in Kent, by the way
parts.note: relations means stories as well as relatives, told by pilgrims on the way to a Kent cathedral city

explanation.surface: Someone casually mentions having elderly relatives down in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's pilgrims tell old stories on the road to the cathedral city in Kent.

clue.text: Flower that blooms in the spring — or autumn

definitions.text: Flower that blooms in the spring — or autumn

parts.words: Flower that blooms in the spring — or autumn
parts.note: a plain description of a small bulb plant, with the twist that some varieties flower in autumn rather than spring

explanation.definitionFit: This corm-grown bloom is a classic early-spring sight, and saffron-bearing kinds flower in autumn.

clue.text: Their house Mercutio called a plague upon

definitions.text: Their house Mercutio called a plague upon

parts.words: Their house Mercutio called a plague upon
parts.note: dying, Mercutio in Romeo and Juliet cries a plague on both houses, the feuding families of Verona

explanation.definitionFit: Juliet's family is one of the two feuding houses Mercutio curses in Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Garment's border one's seen in church

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition reads garment is

indicators.note: seen in puts the edging and the one's pieces inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a hem is the border of cloth
I is one, plus 's as S

explanation.surface: A dress edging is noticed during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' puts HEM and IS (one is) inside CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose shift or slip worn by women is an item of clothing.

clue.text: Such artificial fibre gives Thorndike's doctor the twitch

parts.note: Russell Thorndike wrote the Doctor Syn smuggler novels
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: Wearing man-made fabric makes a novelist's physician fidget.
explanation.definitionFit: Man-made fibres like nylon are manufactured rather than natural.

clue.text: Withdrawal of Navy's ration — repeated grumbling

indicators.note: repeated asks for the turned-round word to be written out twice
a withdrawal is a pulling back, so the ration word is read backwards

parts.note: the Royal Navy issued sailors a daily tot of rum

explanation.surface: Sailors complain on and on about losing their daily tot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdrawal of' turns RUM into MUR, and 'repeated' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A low continuous complaint is a murmur, as in murmurs of discontent.

clue.text: Sovereign equalled twenty francs

definitions.meaning: a ruler or emperor, here the French emperor
an old French gold coin was worth twenty francs and bore the emperor's name

explanation.surface: A remark about currency: a British gold coin matched twenty French francs in value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sovereign' looks like the British coin, inviting a currency conversion; it is the ruler, and 'equalled' just links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonaparte was an emperor, a supreme ruler, and the French gold twenty-franc piece was named after him.

clue.text: A game of snap with this? Happy idea!

definitions.text: A game of snap with this? Happy idea!

parts.words: A game of snap with this? Happy idea!
parts.note: two people pull a forked chicken bone until it snaps, the one with the bigger piece getting a wish granted, a happy idea

explanation.definitionFit: The forked breastbone of a fowl is pulled apart by two people, and the larger piece earns a wish.

clue.text: Prodigal like a slave getting no second start

indicators.note: getting no says the letter named next is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: slavish means servile, like a slave

indicators.note: start picks the opening letter of the word second

explanation.surface: A spendthrift is servile but never gets a second chance to start again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes the S given by 'second start' (the first letter of second) from SLAVISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigal and lavish both describe someone extravagantly free with money.

clue.text: Condescend, say, to drink from this

indicators.note: say indicates the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: to stoop is to condescend, lower oneself

explanation.surface: Lower yourself, as it were, to drink from a humble cup.
explanation.walkthrough: A stoup is an old word for a drinking vessel or flagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking vessel such as a flagon or tankard is what one drinks from.

clue.text: City's upset about bar — one devoted to luxury

indicators.note: about says the shuffled city letters go around the rest
upset says the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the possessive 's adds an S here
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A city is outraged over a bar run by a pleasure-seeker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles CITYS to SYTIC, and 'about' wraps it round BAR plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-indulgent and pleasure-loving, after the ancient Greek city of Sybaris famed for its luxury.

clue.text: Price reduction, a lure intended for listeners

indicators.note: for listeners says the words are to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a bait meant: a lure is bait, intended is meant

explanation.surface: A discount is offered as a deliberate bait to listeners, like a radio advert.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'a bait meant' runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduction or discount on a price or tax is a formal term for lowering it.

clue.text: Visitor from space bound to lead ring ceremony

parts.note: mete is an old word for a boundary, as in metes and bounds
O is ring-shaped
a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: An alien guest is obliged to head a ring ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to lead' reads as obliged to head; 'bound' is METE, put first.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock from outer space that lands on Earth is an arrival from beyond.

clue.text: Lent cape redesigned for a conjurer's figure

indicators.note: redesigned says the letters are reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: A borrowed cloak is restyled for a stage magician.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-pointed star used in magic rituals is a magician's symbol.

clue.text: Sea Beaver, once the villain of a locked-room mystery

definitions.text: the villain of a locked-room mystery

parts.note: the blue is a poetic name for the sea
beaver was once slang for a beard, and for a bearded man

explanation.surface: A seafaring rodent turns out to be the culprit in a whodunit.
explanation.walkthrough: In the folk tale, the wife-murderer forbids his new bride to open one locked room, which hides his previous wives' bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk tale's murderous husband keeps the bodies of past wives in a forbidden locked chamber, a grim kind of mystery.

clue.text: Free battle in a. French, environment

indicators.note: in, with environment, puts the battle inside the French word

parts.note: une is French for a
Loos was a First World War battle in France, 1915

explanation.surface: A fight takes place in French surroundings and frees someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten or release is to set loose.

clue.text: Thus about to become a philosopher

indicators.note: about says the word for thus goes round the other piece

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone, so the story goes, is on the point of turning into a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' is the container signal and 'to' is a piece; 'become' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Zeno's school, which taught calm endurance of hardship, is a member of that philosophical sect.

clue.text: Sugar controller returns us £1 in the pub

indicators.note: in places the middle pieces inside the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: returns reads the word us backwards

parts.note: taken as written
L is the pound sign's letter, from libra
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A drink in the pub costs a pound, but it controls blood sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns US to SU; £1 gives L (pound) and I (one), all inside INN.
explanation.definitionFit: The pancreatic hormone regulates glucose levels in the blood.

clue.text: Somewhat volcanic boxer?

definitions.meaning: a bowl-shaped mouth of a volcano
whimsically, one who puts things in crates

explanation.surface: A fighter with a fiery temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano's mouth is a bowl-shaped hollow, and a packer who puts goods in boxes could jokingly be named the same.

clue.text: Relax severity concerning days of abstinence

parts.note: re means concerning or about
the forty days before Easter are traditionally kept with fasting

explanation.surface: A decision to ease up on strict fasting rules.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease up or soften a stern stance is to give way, become less harsh.

clue.text: Wrong, French river's a slow mover

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
the Oise is a river in northern France; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A complaint that a river in France flows too sluggishly.
explanation.definitionFit: The shelled reptile is proverbially sluggish, as in the fable of the race with the hare.

clue.text: With little latitude for car-pilot error

indicators.note: an error suggests the letters have gone wrong and need reordering

explanation.surface: A driver or pilot has very little margin for mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'error' rearranges CARPILOT. Latitude here is the geographical measure: the hot zone lies near the equator, at low latitudes.
explanation.definitionFit: Places near the equator have low latitude, and the hot zone between the two tropics is described this way.

clue.text: It's nugatory but sweet

definitions.meaning: something worthless or of no importance, a mere bagatelle
a dessert of sponge, custard, jelly and cream, a British pudding

explanation.surface: Something is of no account, yet still pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A worthless thing is a bauble or bagatelle, and the same word is a British layered dessert of sponge, jelly, custard and cream.

clue.text: Split of stick together? Many go

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
to leave is to go away

explanation.surface: A question whether a group should break up or stay united, while many depart.
explanation.walkthrough: The word has two opposite senses, to split and to stick together, both offered in the question; 'Many go' then builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hack apart with an axe is to divide, and the same verb also means to cling.

clue.text: Army man's sound conductor

definitions.note: here man's stands for man is, so the definition reads as the soldier

indicators.note: sound says the conductor's name is heard, not spelt

parts.note: Sir Malcolm Sargent was a famous British orchestral conductor, long associated with the Proms

explanation.surface: A soldier makes a fine leader of an orchestra, or an electrical wire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conductor' suggests electrical wiring, with 'sound' as an adjective; it is Sir Malcolm Sargent, a British conductor, and 'sound' means said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-commissioned officer rank in the army is held by a soldier.
